prompt: Give the Book class proper equals and hashCode methods based only on its isbn field, so two Book objects with the same ISBN are equal (and deduplicate in a HashSet) even when their titles differ.
explanation: equals and hashCode form a contract: objects that are equal must produce the same hash code, because HashSet and HashMap first jump to a hash bucket and only then call equals. Basing both methods on the same field (isbn) keeps the contract intact, while the instanceof check makes equals safely reject null and non-Book arguments in one step. If hashCode still mixed in the title, equal books could land in different buckets and the HashSet would fail to deduplicate them.
hints: Start equals with: if (this == obj) return true; then if (!(obj instanceof Book)) return false; -- instanceof is false for null, which handles the null case.
After the instanceof check, cast obj to Book and compare only the isbn fields with java.util.Objects.equals.
hashCode must use exactly the fields equals uses: return java.util.Objects.hashCode(isbn).
